absent: Real behavior of consumer, firmware, timestamp, export and ACPI helpers when the library is enabled.
Locking discipline, sleeping constraints and concurrency rules beyond lockdep class provisioning.
Interrupt flow selection, hierarchy translation algorithms and domain allocation details.
Pin range integration with pin control and device tree translation specifics.
Validity bitmap construction and static allocation handling for interrupt lines.

findings.text: When the GPIO library is unavailable the sleeping raw value accessors for single lines and for arrays report success with a neutral zero outcome and treat any observed descriptor collection as a caller error.

Without the library, configuration and inspection helpers return neutral or failure outcomes while flagging unexpected use. Extended configuration and debounce report unimplemented, polarity toggle has no effect, polarity and sleep capability report negative, interrupt conversion and name assignment report invalid argument, sharing reports negative, legacy number conversion yields null in one direction and invalid argument in the other.

Firmware based descriptor acquisition without the library always fails with an unimplemented error. Convenience forms without an explicit position obtain position zero through the indexed form, with device managed and unmanaged forms following the same delegation.
An optional firmware lookup treats absence as a null result rather than an error, while preserving other failures and successful descriptors unchanged.
Descriptor identity comparison without the library always reports inequality and flags any present argument as unexpected.
Hardware timestamp enable and disable without the library report unimplemented, and only flag descriptor presence when the library is compiled out.
ACPI connection parameters carry a table entry selector, a line selector within that entry, and a polarity indication.
An ACPI mapping entry pairs a consumer name with a pointer to parameter entries plus a count, together with a bitmask selecting quirk behaviors for translation.

Three quirk selections occupy successive low bit positions starting at the least significant bit, respectively requesting that restriction information be ignored, that only general input output resources be considered, and that the given pin be treated as a system wide absolute number.
Driver table registration without support reports that the target cannot be reached, removal does nothing, and the device managed registration shares the unreachable report.
User visibility helpers without support report unimplemented for export and link creation, while removal is a silent no operation.

A multi descriptor sleeping update passes through null or error containers unchanged and otherwise forwards the contained count, descriptor list, auxiliary info and value data to the array sleeping update.
Inward line direction is represented by numeric one and outward direction by numeric zero.
Each generic GPIO header defines a unique inclusion guard identifier that prevents multiple processing of its declarations.
An interrupt firmware specifier for GPIO is a union holding either a standard interrupt specifier or, when message signaled interrupt support is enabled, a message allocation record.

A GPIO interrupt description combines a core interrupt implementation pointer and a translation domain with optional hierarchical support. Hierarchy adds a firmware reference, a parent domain, translation from child hardware numbers and types to parent values, optional population of parent allocation arguments, optional line to interrupt conversion, and domain operations.

Parent interrupt handling records a flow routine plus either a shared data pointer or an array of per parent pointers, together with parent count, parent list, per line parent selection, threading selection and a flag choosing between shared and per parent data.

Lifecycle and validity state tracks whether initialization has completed, whether the domain is owned externally and therefore not freed by the core, optional hardware preparation, optional validity bitmap preparation plus stored mask and first number for static allocation, and saved copies of the underlying enable, disable, mask and unmask operations plus default trigger type and flow handler.

A GPIO controller description identifies itself by label, device, parent, firmware reference and owner, and offers driver callbacks for exclusive request and release, direction query and configuration, single and masked value access, extended configuration, interrupt number conversion, debug display, validity initialization, pin range integration and hardware timestamp control.

Numeric and naming state comprises a base number, a line count, an offset, an optional name table and a sleep capability flag, with an embedded interrupt controller description when interrupt support is enabled and device tree translation state including cell count plus instance matching and translation callbacks when that support is enabled.

Interrupt capable chips carry separate lockdep classes for interrupt locking and for resource acquisition. Registration helpers either allocate fresh static classes and forward them to the keyed forms or, in the alternate build, forward null keys.

Iteration helpers walk hardware lines over an explicit range or over the whole controller, duplicating each line label and skipping failures, with filtered variants that only visit lines that currently hold a label. Iteration state is kept in a small record holding a label slot and an index slot.
Interrupt resource wiring is supplied through a helper that expands to request and release hooks for the core interrupt structure.

A setter installs a read only core interrupt implementation into a GPIO interrupt description by storing it as a mutable pointer, while domain attachment without interrupt support warns and reports invalid argument.
A pin range record links into a list and binds a pin control device to an embedded controller range.

Range registration helpers for dense, sparse and group forms report success without further action in the observed configuration, with dense and sparse convenience forms delegating to a common routine, and range removal is a silent no operation.

Without the library, conversions from descriptor to controller or device, base and label queries, lookup by label or firmware reference, and interrupt locking report missing device or invalid failures or null results while flagging use as unexpected, and interrupt unlocking only flags unexpected use.

The interrupt description moves from uninitialized to initialized before its members may be used, and domain ownership selects whether teardown frees the domain internally or leaves it to the external allocator.

The shared data pointer and the per parent array occupy the same storage with the mode flag selecting which view is valid, the array form requiring a non null table sized by the parent count, while the parent list itself remains owned by the driver and is only referenced by the core.

Fallback paths treat any observable descriptor, device or chip argument as a programming error signal via a warning, while still returning safe neutral values or standard negative errors so callers do not dereference absent state.
